stem: Neither the clerk nor the supervisors ___ aware of the new schedule until this morning.
hints: With 'neither ... nor', look at the subject closest to the blank.
The nearer subject is 'the supervisors'. Is that one person or more? Also check the time words 'until this morning'.
Make the verb agree with the nearer subject and use the past tense for 'until this morning'. Pick the choice that does both.

solution.methodName: Find what the blank needs, then pick the form

steps.action: Spot the pattern: 'Neither ... nor' joins two subjects.
Apply the rule: with 'neither ... nor' and 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it.
steps.why: The closer subject decides. You may see this called the proximity rule.

steps.action: Find the nearer subject: 'the supervisors', which is plural.
Check the time: 'until this morning' points to the past.
Reread: 'Neither the clerk nor the supervisors were aware of the new schedule until this morning.'

trapNotes.was: Was agrees with 'the clerk', the first subject. With 'neither ... nor', the verb follows the nearer subject, 'the supervisors', which is plural.
trapNotes.is: Is is singular and present. The nearer subject is plural, and 'until this morning' shows the past.
trapNotes.has been: Has been is singular, and it does not fit 'until this morning', which marks a finished time in the past.
